title: Voter Approval of Updated City Charter
ballot_label: Voter Approval of Updated City Charter. Question: Should voters Approve the updated City Charter?
summary: Asks City of Aurora voters to approve an updated city charter, which has not been amended since 1985. The update would also change Aurora from a strong-mayor (mayor-council) form of government to a council-manager form, in which a city manager appointed by the council handles daily operations, hiring and budget preparation. The mayor would remain a voting council member and presiding officer. The change would take effect January 1, 2027.
yes_means: A yes vote approves the updated City of Aurora charter, including the change to a council-manager form of government.
no_means: A no vote rejects the updated charter, leaving the 1985 charter and the current strong-mayor (mayor-council) form of government in place.

arguments.author: City of Aurora (official ballot title summary)
arguments.statement: The official ballot summary says the Aurora City Council believes the city should move from a strong-mayor to a city manager-council government, to separate volunteer leadership from day-to-day professional administration.
arguments.excerpt: In addition, the City Council believes that the form of government in Aurora should change from its current form strong mayor, to a city manager-council form of government. This change is driven by a desire to separate citizen volunteer leadership from day-to-day professional administration.

source.publisher: Marion County Clerk's Office (Elections), Voters' Pamphlet Nov 3, 2026

collection_notes: yes_means/no_means: Oregon local ballot titles carry no official result-of-vote text, so these are neutral one-sentence descriptions written by the collector, grounded strictly in the official ballot question/summary. Arguments of kind 'explainer' on the YES side quote the rationale that the official ballot title/explanatory statement attributes to the sponsoring governing body; they are not filed pamphlet arguments. No comparable NO-side statement exists in the official text.
